docs.title: Welcome to the jungle
docs.text:
A player wiki for Monkey Quest on the MQReborn server (version 1.7.7, data from 2026-10-01): how the game calculates things, where to get items, and how to progress and build. Every number comes from the live game data, and the formulas were checked in-game.

Build calculator Your level, skill points and filters in; best melee, ranged and utility build out. Guides Progression 1–60, builds, farming and every tip in one place. Mechanics Damage, defence, gear, XP, loot, buffs, pets, enemies and more. Items Every item with real stats, icon and where to get it. Weapons All weapons with stat totals, cooldowns and sources. Zones Every zone: enemies, loot, quests, vendors and the best armour against it. World map How zones connect, and which ones fit your level. Quests Quest trees per tribe, dailies and every quest by level. Monsters Enemy types, their attacks and drops. Vendors Who sells what, and where. Tips Every practical tip on one page.

docs.title: The five things that matter most
docs.text:
• A hit deals your base damage plus the scaled value of the weapon you are using. Base = ability power + all gear damage lines + skill-point bonuses. The weapon value is its scaled blunt + element (scaled_stats in items.json). There is no rounding surprise: the damage number equals the sum. hit = base + weapon.scaled_blunt + weapon.scaled_element Tip: To compare weapons, add each weapon's scaled_stats sum to your base. A higher sum always hits harder.
  • Item level (not the level requirement) drives stats. Rarity adds only about 1–4 % up to Epic; Legendary about +15–19 %; Unique about 2×. Items above level 65 drop to 1 (the stat tables end at 65). Tip: Prefer the highest item level you can equip. Ignore rarity unless it is Legendary or Unique.
  • Blunt damage counts toward every element. Blunt accessories raise the damage of elemental weapons too. Elemental lines add on top. All stats are additive (the original game's system).
  • Kill XP falls off when the enemy is 5 or more levels above OR below you, down to 1 XP. This is intended, to stop farming low zones. The exact curve is unknown. Tip: Fight enemies within ±4 levels of your own.
  • Everyone in a group gets enemy loot, whoever kills. Chests reward every group member. There is no loot voting.

docs.title: How trustworthy is this?
docs.text: Item stats, drop chances, quests and zones come straight from the game data. The damage, defence and badge formulas were measured in-game. Rules marked not confirmed yet or player reports still need a test on MQReborn.

docs.title: Build progression by element
docs.text:
This guide doesn't use fixed checkpoints (level 10, 20, …). For each slot it lists every item that beats everything below its level requirement, so a great level-21 item shows up at 21. Pick the tab for the element you play. Your tribe's skill points boost weapons of that element, and accessory element lines only count for hits of the same element.

How to read it: - A build carries a melee weapon and a ranged one (thrown weapons, slingshots, blasters, staffs and damage zones), so each gets its own rows. The weapon rows show what the build calculator recommends at each level: your hit with that level's best accessories, ranked by time per kill (hits to kill × cooldown) against enemies of that level, so a fast weapon that still kills in two hits can beat a bigger, slower one. The score is the hit; the gain column says how many hits and seconds a kill takes, and what it took before. - Accessories (Ears, Wrist, Tail) are scored as blunt + matching element line; blunt counts for every element. - Armour is scored as defence + resist against this element. Armour of the enemy's tribe resists best (about 115 %), Crossroads armour is neutral (100 %) and other tribes' armour gives about 85 % against that element. - Damage and defence never compete for a slot, so a balanced build simply takes the best of both.

  • A hit deals your base damage plus the scaled value of the weapon you are using. Base = ability power + all gear damage lines + skill-point bonuses. The weapon value is its scaled blunt + element (scaled_stats in items.json). There is no rounding surprise: the damage number equals the sum. hit = base + weapon.scaled_blunt + weapon.scaled_element Tip: To compare weapons, add each weapon's scaled_stats sum to your base. A higher sum always hits harder.
  • Skill points come from levelling up (Badge Book). Every 5 points in a tribe give one badge level. Badge level n gives +75 + 20·(n−1) damage of that tribe's element and +67 + 24·(n−1) defence (confirmed in-game for levels 1–4: 75/67, 95/91, 115/115, 135/139). The tables in the data run to badge level 65 and the server has no 40-point cap. The damage bonus only helps weapons of that element. The defence bonus is base defence and counts against all elements (confirmed in-game: +139 to both Defence and Air defence at badge level 4). You can switch tribes for free. badge = floor(points / 5); dmg_bonus = 75 + 20·(badge−1); def_bonus = 67 + 24·(badge−1) Tip: Put skill points into the tribe whose element your best weapon has. Compare weapons including the bonus (the build calculator does this).
  • Tribe gear splits its value into a blunt or defence line plus an element line: weapons and accessories 80 % blunt + 30 % element, armour 85 % defence + 30 % resist. Crossroads gear is 100 % blunt or defence. Since blunt counts for all elements, tribe gear is worth about 110 % (115 % for armour) of a Crossroads piece of the same level.

docs.title: Build for a specific target
docs.text: The build calculator does this interactively in the browser: enter your level, skill points, target and filters, and it shows the best build, every element side by side, and your upgrade path.

docs.title: Principles (all confirmed)
docs.text:
• Damage per hit = base + weapon stat total. Base = 10 × level + the damage lines of your Ears, Wrist and Tail + skill points. The weapon is the biggest factor, then the three accessories.
  • Blunt counts for every element. You don't need matching elements. Pick the highest stat total. Tribe items are worth about 10 % more than Crossroads items of the same level, because they add an element line.
  • Item level beats rarity. Rarity adds only a few percent below Legendary. The level requirement doesn't affect stats.
  • Defence comes from Hat, Body, Legs and Backpack, plus skill points (which count against all elements). Enemies always deal a level-based minimum, and percentage hazards ignore defence.
  • Element defence: enemies attack with their tribe's element. Match your resist to the zone (for example Air resist against Chim Foo / mist enemies).
  • No set bonuses. Mix pieces freely.
  • Rotate weapons. Each item has its own cooldown and there is no global cooldown.
  • Pets deal a share of the enemy's max HP. That's strongest against high-HP enemies and bosses.

docs.title: Build types
docs.text:
Build Focus Slots to prioritise Damage Highest weapon stat total + three damage accessories Weapon, Ears, Wrist, Tail Survival Highest-defence armour and tribe resist for your zone Hat, Body, Legs, Backpack (Backpack has the highest slot factor) Balanced (recommended while levelling) The best weapon available, then whichever slot gives the biggest stat jump Weapon first, then the weakest slot

Skill points (Badge Book) can be reallocated and tribes switched for free, so you can respec for each zone's element.

  • Skill points come from levelling up (Badge Book). Every 5 points in a tribe give one badge level. Badge level n gives +75 + 20·(n−1) damage of that tribe's element and +67 + 24·(n−1) defence (confirmed in-game for levels 1–4: 75/67, 95/91, 115/115, 135/139). The tables in the data run to badge level 65 and the server has no 40-point cap. The damage bonus only helps weapons of that element. The defence bonus is base defence and counts against all elements (confirmed in-game: +139 to both Defence and Air defence at badge level 4). You can switch tribes for free. badge = floor(points / 5); dmg_bonus = 75 + 20·(badge−1); def_bonus = 67 + 24·(badge−1) Tip: Put skill points into the tribe whose element your best weapon has. Compare weapons including the bonus (the build calculator does this).

To rank weapons for your own level and skill points, use the build calculator.

docs.title: Build calculator
docs.text:
Enter your level and skill points, choose filters, and the page works out your build: a melee and a ranged weapon, a utility item, three accessories and four armour pieces, plus your upgrade path. Results update as you type.

  • By default it makes an overall build: enemies of your level, with armour weighted by the attack elements of the zones around your level. Pick an enemy element or a zone only when you want a build against something specific.
  • Click ✕ next to any item to exclude it and see the next best alternative.
  • Click a row in the build element comparison to build around that element.
  • Your settings are remembered in this browser and kept in the page address, so you can bookmark a build.

This calculator needs JavaScript.

docs.title: How it calculates
docs.text:
It uses the same model as the build progression guide:

  • A hit deals your base damage plus the scaled value of the weapon you are using. Base = ability power + all gear damage lines + skill-point bonuses. The weapon value is its scaled blunt + element (scaled_stats in items.json). There is no rounding surprise: the damage number equals the sum. hit = base + weapon.scaled_blunt + weapon.scaled_element Tip: To compare weapons, add each weapon's scaled_stats sum to your base. A higher sum always hits harder.
  • Skill points come from levelling up (Badge Book). Every 5 points in a tribe give one badge level. Badge level n gives +75 + 20·(n−1) damage of that tribe's element and +67 + 24·(n−1) defence (confirmed in-game for levels 1–4: 75/67, 95/91, 115/115, 135/139). The tables in the data run to badge level 65 and the server has no 40-point cap. The damage bonus only helps weapons of that element. The defence bonus is base defence and counts against all elements (confirmed in-game: +139 to both Defence and Air defence at badge level 4). You can switch tribes for free. badge = floor(points / 5); dmg_bonus = 75 + 20·(badge−1); def_bonus = 67 + 24·(badge−1) Tip: Put skill points into the tribe whose element your best weapon has. Compare weapons including the bonus (the build calculator does this).
  • Armour stats are its scaled defence plus a resist line for tribe armour (e.g. Padded Ninja Hat: 51 defence + 18 Air resist; confirmed in-game). Against a given element, your defence = all defence + resist lines of that element. Against blunt (Crossroads) attackers, every resist line counts. The stats window's general "Defence" also includes all resist lines, and each element's defence counts only its own resist lines. def_vs(E) = base_def + Σ armour.defence + Σ armour.resist[E] + badge_def; def_vs(blunt) = base_def + Σ armour.(defence + resist) + badge_def Tip: Wear armour of the enemy's tribe. It resists their element and still counts fully against blunt attacks.
  • Weapon side effects work on MQReborn: Stun Flower stuns 4 s (cooldown 10 s) and Dragon Mace 1 s; Snake Staff (150 % over 10 s, plus its impact hit), Scorpion Sword (150 % over 30 s) and Rotten Stick (25 % over 5 s) poison; Turkey Mace (10 %), Flytrap Staff and Voodoo Doll (15 % in live data, 20 % in patch 1.7.5) steal life. Healing Staff heals 25 % of your HP every 20 s (self only); Horn of Heroism gives +250 elemental defence for 25 s every 30 s; Smoke Bomb gives 15 s of invisibility. A build is a melee weapon, a ranged weapon and one utility item chosen for its role, not for its damage. Not confirmed yet: whether poison is a % of the whole hit or only its earth part; whether Drop bombs (Stink Bombs) hurt enemies. Tip: Open fights against tough enemies with a stun (Stun Flower) and finish with your fastest weapon: a 4 s stun covers about 8 swings of a 0.5 s weapon. Use the build calculator's utility slot to compare roles.

Weapons are ranked by time per kill (hits to kill × cooldown, at least 0.5 s), so a fast weapon that one-shots beats a slow one that hits harder. Damage zones count 50 % of their damage per tick. Damage and defence never compete for a slot, so the best accessories and the best armour are picked independently.

The build element is what your accessories and badges boost. Element lines on accessories only count for weapons of the same element, but blunt counts for all of them, so the best melee and ranged weapons can have different elements. For an overall build, each armour resist line is weighted by the share of nearby zones where it counts (zones of its own element plus Crossroads zones, whose enemies deal blunt damage).

The utility slot is valued per role against your build rather than by damage: free hits of your main weapon during a stun, poison damage per use, HP healed per second, elemental damage saved per hit, or seconds of invisibility. "Automatic" picks the first role that has an item you don't already use, in the order crowd control, damage over time, sustain, defence buff, escape.

docs.title: Rules that matter for farming
docs.text:
• Enemies drop loot with a 25 % base chance (higher with more stars). The drop comes from a weighted merge of a generic (Crossroads) table and the enemy's tribe table, plus species-specific parts. Tier odds by enemy level: 20–39 → T1 66 % / T2 33 %; 40+ → T1 30 % / T2 60 % / T3 10 %.
  • Everyone in a group gets enemy loot, whoever kills. Chests reward every group member. There is no loot voting.
  • Polished/Refined Shadow Shards drop only from spawners in high-level trails (Forbidden Keep and up).
  • Jack-in-the-boxes only work on highways, Crossroads Path and the event area. The ones inside trails are disabled on purpose.
  • Elixirs of Wealth give +50 % bananas, but not on bananas from selling items.
  • Playing close together in a group gives a banana multiplier.
  • Being knocked out costs some of the bananas you picked up in the trail since your last checkpoint. Quest and selling bananas are safe. You wait 5 s to respawn, then get brief invincibility. Long buffs (e.g. Wisdom) survive death. Tip: Reach checkpoints before risky fights.

Group farming is strictly better: everyone gets enemy and chest loot, kill XP is shared, and the group banana multiplier applies.

docs.title: How to level efficiently
docs.text:
1. Quests first. They pay most of your XP; idol-collector achievements (25k–100k XP) and the Warrior Games (10 rewarded runs per day, scaled to your level) come next.
  2. Fight enemies within ±4 levels of your own. Kill XP falls toward 1 for enemies 5+ levels away, above or below. Group kills share XP.
  3. Upgrade your weapon whenever you can. Your hit damage is your base plus the weapon's stat total, so a better weapon is the biggest single jump in power.
  4. Use Elixirs of Wisdom (+20 %) during long quest or kill sessions. They don't boost achievement XP.
  5. Stay at or above a zone's level. Under-levelled players get one-shot even with good defence.

The level cap is 60. Each level adds +10 ability power, +10 defence and +100 max HP, plus skill points for the Badge Book.

  • Kill XP falls off when the enemy is 5 or more levels above OR below you, down to 1 XP. This is intended, to stop farming low zones. The exact curve is unknown. Tip: Fight enemies within ±4 levels of your own.
  • Being below a zone's recommended level gets you one-shot even with good defence (e.g. 340 defence, 1,400 HP in the Forbidden Keep arena). Tip: Stay at or above the recommended level of a trail.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
Each tip comes from a game rule on the mechanics pages.

  • Don't count on idol achievements for idols collected before level 3. Achievements only count progress from level 3. "(Daily)" achievements are not implemented yet, so they pay only once.
  • Don't judge buffs by the stats window. Resist and shield buffs work (Horn of Heroism: +250 all elemental resists for 25 s, 30 s cooldown; Potions of Shielding). The stats window does not show them. (player reports)
  • Reach checkpoints before risky fights. Being knocked out costs some of the bananas you picked up in the trail since your last checkpoint. Quest and selling bananas are safe. You wait 5 s to respawn, then get brief invincibility. Long buffs (e.g. Wisdom) survive death.
  • Wear armour of the enemy's tribe. It resists their element and still counts fully against blunt attacks. Armour stats are its scaled defence plus a resist line for tribe armour (e.g. Padded Ninja Hat: 51 defence + 18 Air resist; confirmed in-game). Against a given element, your defence = all defence + resist lines of that element. Against blunt (Crossroads) attackers, every resist line counts. The stats window's general "Defence" also includes all resist lines, and each element's defence counts only its own resist lines.
  • Stay at or above the recommended level of a trail. Being below a zone's recommended level gets you one-shot even with good defence (e.g. 340 defence, 1,400 HP in the Forbidden Keep arena).
  • To compare weapons, add each weapon's scaled_stats sum to your base. A higher sum always hits harder. A hit deals your base damage plus the scaled value of the weapon you are using. Base = ability power + all gear damage lines + skill-point bonuses. The weapon value is its scaled blunt + element (scaled_stats in items.json). There is no rounding surprise: the damage number equals the sum.
  • Wear the resist that matches the zone's tribe. Enemies attack with their tribe's element. The matching resist protects you: mist (Chim Foo/Shadow) enemies → Air resist. Tribes and elements: Bone=Earth, Outlaw=Fire, Shadow=Air, Wild=Ice, Grease=Lightning.
  • Put skill points into the tribe whose element your best weapon has. Compare weapons including the bonus (the build calculator does this). Skill points come from levelling up (Badge Book). Every 5 points in a tribe give one badge level. Badge level n gives +75 + 20·(n−1) damage of that tribe's element and +67 + 24·(n−1) defence (confirmed in-game for levels 1–4: 75/67, 95/91, 115/115, 135/139). The tables in the data run to badge level 65 and the server has no 40-point cap. The damage bonus only helps weapons of that element. The defence bonus is base defence and counts against all elements (confirmed in-game: +139 to both Defence and Air defence at badge level 4). You can switch tribes for free.
  • Prefer the highest item level you can equip. Ignore rarity unless it is Legendary or Unique. Item level (not the level requirement) drives stats. Rarity adds only about 1–4 % up to Epic; Legendary about +15–19 %; Unique about 2×. Items above level 65 drop to 1 (the stat tables end at 65).
  • Heal or jump right after loading into those trails. Known recurring bug: entering some trails (Mushroom Hollow ↔ Swamp of Misery, Lost Fortress, Bonsai Peaks …) can knock you out or take most of your HP. Healing may stay disabled until a real death or a restart.
  • Open fights against tough enemies with a stun (Stun Flower) and finish with your fastest weapon: a 4 s stun covers about 8 swings of a 0.5 s weapon. Use the build calculator's utility slot to compare roles. Weapon side effects work on MQReborn: Stun Flower stuns 4 s (cooldown 10 s) and Dragon Mace 1 s; Snake Staff (150 % over 10 s, plus its impact hit), Scorpion Sword (150 % over 30 s) and Rotten Stick (25 % over 5 s) poison; Turkey Mace (10 %), Flytrap Staff and Voodoo Doll (15 % in live data, 20 % in patch 1.7.5) steal life. Healing Staff heals 25 % of your HP every 20 s (self only); Horn of Heroism gives +250 elemental defence for 25 s every 30 s; Smoke Bomb gives 15 s of invisibility. A build is a melee weapon, a ranged weapon and one utility item chosen for its role, not for its damage. Not confirmed yet: whether poison is a % of the whole hit or only its earth part; whether Drop bombs (Stink Bombs) hurt enemies.
  • Fight enemies within ±4 levels of your own. Kill XP falls off when the enemy is 5 or more levels above OR below you, down to 1 XP. This is intended, to stop farming low zones. The exact curve is unknown.

docs.title: More
docs.text:
• To compare weapons, use their stat totals on the item pages, not the inventory stat (it only shows your best hotbar weapon).
  • Buffs work even when the stats window doesn't show them.
  • Heal or jump right after loading into Mushroom Hollow, Swamp of Misery, Lost Fortress or Bonsai Peaks (known entry bug).
  • Collect idols only from level 3 on; achievements don't count earlier.
  • The Healing Staff only heals you. Deselect teammates before using it.

docs.text:

docs.title: Buffs and healing
docs.text:
• Elixir of Wisdom: +20 % XP (not on achievement XP).
  • Elixir of Wealth: +50 % bananas (not when selling).
  • Horn of Heroism: +250 to all elemental resists for 25 s, 30 s cooldown.
  • Potion of Shielding: damage reduction.
  • Scrying Orb: turns you invisible and lets you see and hit invisible enemies.
  • Healing Staff: heals 25 % of max HP on a 20 s cooldown, on yourself only.
  • Food and potions heal fixed amounts, some over time. Healing power doesn't affect them.

The stats window does not show active resist or shield buffs, but they work.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Whether damage elixirs (e.g. Elixir of Fire, +25 fire for 5 min) raise hit damage is not confirmed. (not confirmed yet)
  • Only one buff of each type is active at a time. A new buff of the same type replaces the old one if it is at least as strong, even if it is shorter. (not confirmed on MQReborn yet)
  • Resist and shield buffs work (Horn of Heroism: +250 all elemental resists for 25 s, 30 s cooldown; Potions of Shielding). The stats window does not show them. Tip: Don't judge buffs by the stats window. (player reports)
  • Elixirs of Wealth give +50 % bananas, but not on bananas from selling items.
  • Elixirs of Wisdom give +20 % XP for their duration (Minor 10 min … Ultimate 6 h). They do not apply to achievement XP. Temporary XP events stack additively.
  • Food and potions heal fixed amounts (or heal over time, in ticks every 3 s). Healing power does not affect consumables.
  • The Healing Staff heals 25 % of your max HP on a 20 s cooldown, on yourself only (it fails if a teammate is selected).
  • Each item has its own cooldown (cooldown_time in items.json). There is no global cooldown, so rotating several weapons or consumables keeps damage flowing.

All consumables with their effects: consumables.

docs.title: The formula (confirmed in-game)
docs.text:
hit damage = your base damage + weapon stat total
base damage = ability power (10 × level) + all gear damage lines (blunt + element) + skill-point bonuses
weapon stat total = the weapon's scaled blunt + element (see each weapon's page)

Worked example (measured 2026-10-01): a level-22 player had a base of 516. - Silver Stars (stat total 227) hit for 743 = 516 + 227. - Bo Staff (stat total 305) hit for 821 = 516 + 305.

How to compare weapons: a higher stat total always means a harder hit. Divide by the cooldown to estimate damage over time. The weapons list shows every weapon's stat total.

The stats window is misleading

Your inventory damage stat shows your base plus only your strongest hotbar weapon. It doesn't show how hard your other weapons hit.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Ability power (part of base damage) is 10 × your level. AP(L) = 10·L
  • Blunt damage counts toward every element. Blunt accessories raise the damage of elemental weapons too. Elemental lines add on top. All stats are additive (the original game's system).
  • A weapon's catalog effect value (the 'bonus damage' in old patch notes, e.g. Silver Stars +50 air) is NOT added to hits. It only defines special effects such as life steal %, poison %, stun and the underwater bonus.
  • Boom/TNT barrels can only be broken with fire-element weapons.
  • A hit deals your base damage plus the scaled value of the weapon you are using. Base = ability power + all gear damage lines + skill-point bonuses. The weapon value is its scaled blunt + element (scaled_stats in items.json). There is no rounding surprise: the damage number equals the sum. hit = base + weapon.scaled_blunt + weapon.scaled_element Tip: To compare weapons, add each weapon's scaled_stats sum to your base. A higher sum always hits harder.
  • Ground melee hits everything in a box 3.6 units in front of you and 1 unit high, all at once. Ranged shots fly straight at about 10 units/s for 3 s and stop at walls (terrain collision since 1.6). (not confirmed on MQReborn yet)
  • Every successful hit deals at least 1 damage. (not confirmed on MQReborn yet)
  • There are no critical hits, misses or dodges. A hit lands when the attack box overlaps the enemy on the same plane. Apparent misses are lag or desync. (not confirmed on MQReborn yet)
  • The inventory damage stat shows your base plus only the strongest weapon on your hotbar (by scaled sum). It does not tell you how hard your other weapons hit.
  • Super stomp damage depends only on your level, not on gear. stomp = ceil(10·L + 20) · 2 (not confirmed on MQReborn yet)
  • Zone weapons (gas clouds) deal 50 % of your total damage per tick. The in-game tooltip shows 1/3. tick = 0.5 · (base + weapon.scaled_sum)
  • Weapon side effects work on MQReborn: Stun Flower stuns 4 s (cooldown 10 s) and Dragon Mace 1 s; Snake Staff (150 % over 10 s, plus its impact hit), Scorpion Sword (150 % over 30 s) and Rotten Stick (25 % over 5 s) poison; Turkey Mace (10 %), Flytrap Staff and Voodoo Doll (15 % in live data, 20 % in patch 1.7.5) steal life. Healing Staff heals 25 % of your HP every 20 s (self only); Horn of Heroism gives +250 elemental defence for 25 s every 30 s; Smoke Bomb gives 15 s of invisibility. A build is a melee weapon, a ranged weapon and one utility item chosen for its role, not for its damage. Not confirmed yet: whether poison is a % of the whole hit or only its earth part; whether Drop bombs (Stink Bombs) hurt enemies. Tip: Open fights against tough enemies with a stun (Stun Flower) and finish with your fastest weapon: a 4 s stun covers about 8 swings of a 0.5 s weapon. Use the build calculator's utility slot to compare roles.

docs.title: Elements
docs.text: Blunt counts for every element, so your total damage matters more than matching elements. Each tribe item also gets an element line on top. Weapons and accessories get 80 % blunt + 30 % element, so tribe gear is worth about 110 % of a Crossroads piece of the same level. See Gear and stats.

docs.title: Death and hazards
docs.text:
• Knock-out:
  • You lose some of the bananas you picked up in the trail since your last checkpoint. Quest and selling bananas are safe.
  • You wait 5 s to respawn, then get brief invincibility.
  • Long buffs survive.
  • Hazards (lava, spikes, smashers) take a percentage of your max HP and ignore defence.
  • Drowning starts when the air meter runs out. Water-breathing potions help.

Known bug

Entering some trails (Mushroom Hollow ↔ Swamp of Misery, Lost Fortress, Bonsai Peaks) can knock you out or take most of your HP. Heal or jump right after loading in.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Being knocked out costs some of the bananas you picked up in the trail since your last checkpoint. Quest and selling bananas are safe. You wait 5 s to respawn, then get brief invincibility. Long buffs (e.g. Wisdom) survive death. Tip: Reach checkpoints before risky fights.
  • Drowning damage starts when the air meter runs out. Its timing changed several times and is "not fully fixed". Water-breathing potions do affect it on MQReborn.
  • Environmental hazards (lava, spikes, smashers) deal a percentage of your max HP (often about 10 % per tick) and ignore defence. Stompers can hit more than once. (player reports)
  • Known recurring bug: entering some trails (Mushroom Hollow ↔ Swamp of Misery, Lost Fortress, Bonsai Peaks …) can knock you out or take most of your HP. Healing may stay disabled until a real death or a restart. Tip: Heal or jump right after loading into those trails.

docs.title: Defence and elements
docs.text: Your defence = 10 × level (base) + armour (Hat, Body, Legs, Backpack) + skill-point defence. Defence reduces enemy attack damage, but enemies always deal at least a level-based minimum. Hazards that take a percentage of your max HP ignore defence completely.

docs.title: Elements and tribes
docs.text:
Tribe Element Resist that protects you Bone (Ootu) Earth Earth resist Outlaw (Sea Dragons) Fire Fire resist Shadow (Chim Foo, mist enemies) Air Air resist Wild Ice Ice resist Grease Lightning Lightning resist Crossroads none (blunt) Defence

Enemies attack with their tribe's element, so wear the resist that matches the zone you are in.

docs.title: Badge Book (skill points)
docs.text:
Every 5 skill points in a tribe give one badge level. The damage bonus applies to weapons of that tribe's element. The defence bonus counts against all elements according to the team.

Skill points in the tribe Badge level Element damage bonus Defence bonus 5 1 75 67 10 2 95 91 15 3 115 115 20 4 135 139 25 5 155 163 30 6 175 187 35 7 195 211 40 8 215 235 45 9 235 259 50 10 255 283 55 11 275 307 60 12 295 331 75 15 355 403 100 20 455 523

Same numbers for every element (Air, Earth, Fire, Ice, Lightning). Confirmed in-game for badge levels 1–4.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Base defence is 10 × level. Armour adds to it. Base max HP is 100 × level. Def(L) = 10·L; HP(L) = 100·L
  • Defence reduces damage from enemy attacks, but enemies always deal at least a level-based minimum. Percentage-of-max-HP hazards ignore defence.
  • Armour stats are its scaled defence plus a resist line for tribe armour (e.g. Padded Ninja Hat: 51 defence + 18 Air resist; confirmed in-game). Against a given element, your defence = all defence + resist lines of that element. Against blunt (Crossroads) attackers, every resist line counts. The stats window's general "Defence" also includes all resist lines, and each element's defence counts only its own resist lines. def_vs(E) = base_def + Σ armour.defence + Σ armour.resist[E] + badge_def; def_vs(blunt) = base_def + Σ armour.(defence + resist) + badge_def Tip: Wear armour of the enemy's tribe. It resists their element and still counts fully against blunt attacks.
  • Being below a zone's recommended level gets you one-shot even with good defence (e.g. 340 defence, 1,400 HP in the Forbidden Keep arena). Tip: Stay at or above the recommended level of a trail.
  • Enemies attack with their tribe's element. The matching resist protects you: mist (Chim Foo/Shadow) enemies → Air resist. Tribes and elements: Bone=Earth, Outlaw=Fire, Shadow=Air, Wild=Ice, Grease=Lightning. Tip: Wear the resist that matches the zone's tribe.
  • Skill points come from levelling up (Badge Book). Every 5 points in a tribe give one badge level. Badge level n gives +75 + 20·(n−1) damage of that tribe's element and +67 + 24·(n−1) defence (confirmed in-game for levels 1–4: 75/67, 95/91, 115/115, 135/139). The tables in the data run to badge level 65 and the server has no 40-point cap. The damage bonus only helps weapons of that element. The defence bonus is base defence and counts against all elements (confirmed in-game: +139 to both Defence and Air defence at badge level 4). You can switch tribes for free. badge = floor(points / 5); dmg_bonus = 75 + 20·(badge−1); def_bonus = 67 + 24·(badge−1) Tip: Put skill points into the tribe whose element your best weapon has. Compare weapons including the bonus (the build calculator does this).

docs.title: Economy and travel
docs.text:
• Currencies: bananas (earned in game) and MonkeyCash (MC; from dailies, achievements and level-ups).
  • Vendors sell at the catalog price and buy back at the sell price.
  • A group playing close together gets a banana multiplier.
  • Fast travel: level 5 to start, level 10 to leave Crossroads, level 15 for tribe highways, and 10 idols for a trail. Travelling to a group member ignores idols.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Playing close together in a group gives a banana multiplier.
  • Vendors charge the catalog price × amount and buy back at the sell price × amount (bananas or MonkeyCash per item). Item sales (temporary discounts) exist since 1.7.7. (not confirmed on MQReborn yet)
  • Fast travel needs level 5 (level 10 to leave Crossroads, level 15 for tribe highways) and 10 idols for trails. Travelling to a group member ignores idols.
  • There is a single US game server, and desync is common. Re-entering a level fixes most enemy and hitbox desync.

Vendors and their stock: vendors.

docs.title: Enemies
docs.text:
• An enemy's HP and attack depend on its level, not its type. Its level is the zone's difficulty plus a small per-placement offset.
  • Enemy defence is 0.
  • Starred enemies are tougher and drop more.
  • Invisible enemies need Scrying Orb detection.
  • Spawners break in 3 hits.
  • Enemy types differ in behaviour: detection range, speed, and whether they shoot.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Invisible enemies (and invisible quest objects) can only be seen and damaged with the Scrying Orb's detection.
  • An enemy's HP and damage come from its level (zone difficulty + a per-placement offset), not from its type. Enemy defence is 0 at every level in the live data.
  • Damage over time (poison) does not make enemies aggressive.
  • Spawners break in 3 hits.
  • Starred enemies are tougher versions with a higher drop chance (more stars, better drops).

docs.title: Gear and stats
docs.text:
Item stats are computed, not printed. The game derives each item's stats from: - its item level, which is not the same as its level requirement; - its rarity, slot, tribe and weapon type.

The catalog numbers you might find elsewhere are tuning values for special effects, not stats. Every item page shows the real stats. They are confirmed in-game to match exactly.

docs.title: Slots
docs.text: Slot Gives Weapons (hotbar) Damage (stat total added to each hit) Ears, Wrist, Tail Damage (added to your base; about 12 % of a same-level weapon each) Hat (Hair), Body, Legs, Backpack Defence (Backpack slightly more than the others) Head, Upper face, Lower face Nothing (decoration) Vanity (costume) Nothing

docs.title: What makes an item strong
docs.text:
1. Item level. Stats grow quickly with item level. An item with a high item level and a low requirement is a bargain.
  2. Tribe. Tribe items add an element line on top: about 110 % of a Crossroads item (115 % for armour).
  3. Rarity matters little: Common → Epic is only about +1–4 %. Legendary adds about 15–19 % and Unique about 2×.
  4. Items above item level 65 drop to 1, because the stat tables end at 65.

Browse by slot: Hat · Body · Legs · Backpack · Ears · Wrist · Tail

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• An accessory is worth about 12 % of a same-level weapon's damage (40 % offence ratio × 1/3 slot factor ÷ 110 %).
  • Holding two copies of the same weapon or ability has no gameplay effect.
  • Item level (not the level requirement) drives stats. Rarity adds only about 1–4 % up to Epic; Legendary about +15–19 %; Unique about 2×. Items above level 65 drop to 1 (the stat tables end at 65). Tip: Prefer the highest item level you can equip. Ignore rarity unless it is Legendary or Unique.
  • There are no set bonuses. "Set building" means collecting matching pieces.
  • Weapon and gear stats are computed from item level, rarity, slot, tribe and action type (the original formula). They are not the numbers printed in the catalog. items.json → scaled_stats holds the result. It is confirmed in-game to match exactly.
  • Weapons and accessories (Ears, Wrist, Tail) give damage. Armour (Hair, Body, Legs, Backpack) gives defence. Decorations (Head, Upper face, Lower face) give no stats. Vanity (costume) items give no stats.
  • The team says stats are "not finalized and will not be for some time". Expect rebalances.
  • Tribe gear splits its value into a blunt or defence line plus an element line: weapons and accessories 80 % blunt + 30 % element, armour 85 % defence + 30 % resist. Crossroads gear is 100 % blunt or defence. Since blunt counts for all elements, tribe gear is worth about 110 % (115 % for armour) of a Crossroads piece of the same level.
  • Your tribe does not restrict which weapons or gear you can use. Its effect is the skill-point bonus to its own element, so weapons and gear of your tribe's element benefit most.

docs.title: Loot
docs.text:
• Enemies: 25 % base drop chance, higher on starred enemies. Each drop comes from a generic table plus the enemy's tribe table, plus species-specific parts. Higher-level enemies roll better tiers.
  • Chests and objects: each loot table rolls by weight. Zone pages list the best chance per item.
  • Groups: everyone in a group gets enemy loot and chest loot. There is no voting.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• In a chest's loot table, the chance of an item is its weight ÷ the total weight. drop_tables.json → chance_per_pick. P(item) = weight / Σ weights (not confirmed on MQReborn yet)
  • Enemies drop loot with a 25 % base chance (higher with more stars). The drop comes from a weighted merge of a generic (Crossroads) table and the enemy's tribe table, plus species-specific parts. Tier odds by enemy level: 20–39 → T1 66 % / T2 33 %; 40+ → T1 30 % / T2 60 % / T3 10 %.
  • Everyone in a group gets enemy loot, whoever kills. Chests reward every group member. There is no loot voting.
  • Jack-in-the-boxes only work on highways, Crossroads Path and the event area. The ones inside trails are disabled on purpose.
  • A super-rare 4-piece armour set drops from high-level, high-star enemies.
  • Polished/Refined Shadow Shards drop only from spawners in high-level trails (Forbidden Keep and up).

Item pages list every known source (vendor, recipe, quest reward, enemy drop, chest).

docs.title: Pets
docs.text:
• Attack pets deal a share of the enemy's max HP per hit (the "stat ratio"), whatever your gear. The strongest deal over 100 % of max HP per use, which makes pets excellent against high-HP enemies.
  • Shield pets: Croaker takes about 75 % off incoming damage (hazards included). Gravewing blocks damage while it attacks.
  • Heal pets heal a share of your max HP.
  • A pet can count as the second player on 2-player co-op gates.
  • Each pet ability has a cooldown and uses pet energy. Energy refills over time.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• A pet can count as the second player on 2-player co-op gates. Pets can also damage some targets that weapons can't.
  • Pet attacks deal a percentage of the enemy's max HP per hit (itemEffectStatRatio in pet_abilities.json), regardless of your gear. Strong pets do over 100 % per use. (not confirmed on MQReborn yet)
  • Croaker's shield takes about 75 % off incoming damage, hazards included. Gravewing's shield blocks damage while the pet attacks. (player reports)

All pets with their ability numbers: pets.

Whether MQReborn caps pet damage on bosses is still open.

docs.title: Quests and achievements
docs.text:
• You can hold one quest per NPC at a time.
  • Collect objectives count only items picked up while the quest is active.
  • Crafting objectives require crafting the item yourself.
  • Dailies reset at 00:00 UTC.
  • Achievements count only from level 3. "(Daily)" achievements pay once.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Dailies reset at 00:00 UTC. The server restarts at the reset.
  • You can hold one quest per NPC at a time. Collect objectives only count items picked up while the quest is active. Crafting objectives require crafting the item yourself. A quest edited by a patch keeps its old objectives if you had already accepted it. Recipe fixes don't apply to recipes you already learned.
  • Achievements only count progress from level 3. "(Daily)" achievements are not implemented yet, so they pay only once. Tip: Don't count on idol achievements for idols collected before level 3.

All quests by level: quests. Each quest page links its objectives, rewards, prerequisites and follow-ups.

docs.title: XP and levels
docs.text:
• The level cap is 60.
  • Each level gives +10 ability power, +10 defence, +100 max HP and skill points.
  • Kill enemies within ±4 levels of your own. Further away in either direction, kill XP falls off toward 1.
  • The big XP sources are quests, dailies, idol-collector achievements (25k–100k XP) and the Warrior Games (10 rewarded runs per day, scaled to your level).
  • Elixirs of Wisdom add +20 % to everything except achievement XP.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• In a group, kill XP goes to every member, weighted by each member's own level (not just the killing blow).
  • Kill XP falls off when the enemy is 5 or more levels above OR below you, down to 1 XP. This is intended, to stop farming low zones. The exact curve is unknown. Tip: Fight enemies within ±4 levels of your own.
  • The main XP sources are quests (rebalanced 1.6.4.1: more XP mid-game), dailies, idol-collector achievements (25k–100k XP each) and the Warrior Games.
  • The level cap is 60.
  • Each level gives +10 ability power, +10 defence, +100 max HP and skill points. The level-up menu shows the changes and grants an MC Mall item every 5 levels.
  • Warrior Games runs grant real XP and items. XP scales with your level (since 1.7.5.1), limited to 10 rewarded runs per day. Level 60 gets the level-50 loot table on purpose.

docs.title: Quests and questlines
docs.text: The in-game Quest Journal, laid out exactly like the game does it (its layout code, ported). Story lines run left to right along the top; side, co-op and follow-up lines branch off below them. Drag the map to move around, pick a questline on the left to jump to it, switch tribes with the tabs. Hover a node for the quest, click it to open it. Title colours: story, primary, side quest, co-op. Dailies and events are not in the journal; they are listed below.

docs.title: World map
docs.text: The in-game world map: the World of Ook overview and the map of each tribe region, with the game's own art and layout. On a region map the trail connects every place, and its exit (the globe) leads to the highways. On the Ook map the highways link the regions, and the crests mark where each region's trail joins a highway. Hover a place for its level, click it to open the zone, and click a map, a tab, a crest or the globe to switch maps.
